messages:
dario: quick heads-up - onboarding halcyon-22b int4a with tiled-prefill exposed a reproducible checksum delta tied to shard-rollover during pack/unpack. divergence always happens right after a rollover event when token index % 11023 == 0. smallest repro below.

emily: interesting, 11023 is a weird non-power boundary. can you paste the run flags and a tiny log?

dario: repro run:
```
./onboard.sh --model halcyon-22b --quant int4a --context 45000 --prefill tiled --kv-tile=4096 --kv-rollover-threshold=11023 --seed 2026 --kv-debug=trace
```
log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-26T10:11:00Z] prefill.tiled len=45000 tile=4096 rollover.threshold=11023
[2026-03-26T10:11:34Z] kv.checksum(oracle)=0xa1b2c3d4
[2026-03-26T10:11:34Z] kv.checksum(live)=0xa1b2c35e  <-- split after rollover seq=27 token_idx=11023
```
I also see a PACK_PARITY mismatch in the trace: pack parity flipped to odd on live path but oracle stayed even.

rod: PACK_PARITY flip? sounds like pack/unpack path has a non-deterministic branch when rollover hits a fragment smaller than PACK_CHUNK. maybe unpack uses a vectorized tail path that misaligns low-order bytes under int4 packing. did you try FORCE_PACK_TAIL=scalar?

dario: not yet, good idea. will try FORCE_PACK_TAIL=scalar + ASYNC_KV_FLUSH=0. also grabbed pack/unpack hex dumps around the rollover window and uploaded to artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/eng-ml/halcyon/rollover-dump-27.tar.gz

mira: also check SHARD_ROLLOUT=stagger vs all-sync. if different shards apply rollover at slightly different times, parity/state might diverge depending on which shard hits the vector tail path first. try SHARD_ROLLOUT=sync.

emily: add a control run with FP16 runtime (no quant kernels) to rule out packing math. if fp16 matches oracle then quant packing is prime suspect.

dario: queued three local jobs: 1) FORCE_PACK_TAIL=scalar 2) ASYNC_KV_FLUSH=0 + SHARD_ROLLOUT=sync 3) FP16 fallback. infra-bot, please queue CI variants.

infra-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17599 (force-pack-tail)
infra-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17600 (sync-rollout+sync-flush)
infra-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17601 (fp16-fallback)

jeff: small nit - pack parity flipping could also be correlated with our new PACK_ALIGNMENT_OPT that tries to align across NVSHMEM boundaries. try PACK_ALIGNMENT_OPT=off to see if it stabilizes.

rod: also create a tiny deterministic unit test: replay first 11.5k tokens (one rollover) on single-shard pinned run and assert kv.checksum equal between oracle and live. that'll let us bisect vectorized tail vs normal path quickly.

dario: making that unit test now. plan: reproduce locally, bisect on PACK_ALIGNMENT_OPT / PACK_PARITY code paths, then run a kernel-level memory-check (valgrind-like) on unpack tail.

emily: if unpack tail is to blame, suspect a mis-sized memcpy or an off-by-one in the vector tail loop which only manifests when rollover fragment size % 8 != 0 under int4 nibble packing.

mira: agreed. capture the exact fragment lengths at rollover (you uploaded hex dumps) and compare both pack/unpack outputs byte-by-byte. also include ropestate and kvsync logs in artifacts.

dario: will post diffs from the byte-level compare and unit test results in ~45m. thanks all. :construction_worker:
